header.name: Organizations: An Anthropological Perspective
header.description:
Where would you like to work?
Imagine coming to IIITD or any such institution where you find your batch mates, professors and others being excited about their work. Discussions are all around the next thing that's going to change the world, the atmosphere is vibrant, lively and exciting. People are proud of their work. You see people work together, solve problems together, set standards, share ideas on how to improve performance and value diversity. You are given an opportunity to rise and shine.
Now imagine the same place being very toxic, where people are very insecure, secretive, highly competitive with no cooperation etc. or a place where both of these co-exist…a sort of a hybrid
So, where would you like to be?
We live in a world which is more or less organized. We live most of our lives within organizations and sometimes amongst them. We grow and live in families and kin groups of different sorts, study in educational institutions, work for firms or public agencies of different sizes and shapes, join clubs, service organizations etc. and infact, if we take a moment to reflect, we would understand that a large part of our lives have been shaped by organizations.
Now, getting back to the earlier question…while everyone wants to work for an ideal organisation where you have opportunities to rise and shine and come to work/study everyday in a pleasant setting…achieving this kind of a cultural setting is every leader’s dream and is easier said than done.
Managing and setting ideals to create such a work culture requires understanding the various factors (both internal and external) that affect the organisation. Social and cultural influences do play a significant role more than what we tend to acknowledge. In the recent past corporations have started using ethnography and anthropology to gain insights into managing organizations strategically. Exploring and deconstructing such cultural and social influences through both fieldwork and case studies (text and videos) with a sprinkling of anthropological theories is the primary intent of this course.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: This course through case study analyses will nudge learners to delve deeper into the social and cultural factors that influence and shape organizations today.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Through ethnographic case studies and fieldwork, the learner will be able to apply and incorporate ideas of correlating significant but seemingly tiny clues to a larger organizational canvas.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The learner would be able to apply knowledge gleaned from this course onto organizations thus converting class material to practical insights.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: The learner will be able to present collaborative team work to an audience in a creative and easily accessible format.
